finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL server-side. The only check is that the string starts with 'https://'. The host is never validated, and redirects are followed by default, so the request can reach internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10), attacker-controlled JSON body on an unauthenticated route

trace.note: Unauthenticated POST /profile/avatar handler; no auth middleware is registered on the app (only express.json at line 5).
Only check: typeof string and url.startsWith('https://'). No parsing of the URL, no host/IP allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local/metadata block.
axios.get(url) is called with the unvalidated URL. axios follows redirects by default and does not re-check targets.
Response size (img.data.length) is returned to the attacker, so there is at least a length oracle on the internal response.

finding.guards_checked: (1) typeof === 'string' – passes for any string. (2) startsWith('https://') – satisfied by https://<any host>, e.g. https://127.0.0.1, https://10.0.0.5, https://internal-service, https://attacker.example that 302s to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (scheme change on redirect is not checked, so the http-only metadata endpoint is reachable). Not a bypass concern: no DNS/IP pinning, so DNS rebinding also works. No timeout or maxContentLength is set, which is a resource issue only and not reported separately. Route /users/:id (server.js:18-21) is not an SSRF: the host is the constant USER_SVC and the id is encodeURIComponent'd, so the attacker cannot change host or scheme (the path can still be shaped with '..', but that stays on users.internal).

verdict.guard_found: none. server.js:11 only checks typeof === "string" and url.startsWith("https://"), which is a prefix check and does not close the finding. No auth middleware is registered: server.js:5 is only express.json(). No host or IP validation exists anywhere on the path before the sink at server.js:14.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10) reaches axios.get at server.js:14 on an unauthenticated route (server.js:9), and the only check (server.js:11) is an https:// prefix test, so an attacker can point it at internal hosts or a redirecting https URL to the plain-http metadata endpoint, since axios follows redirects by default.
